headline: War at sea keeps oil above $100 as Canada's job market slips
summary: Iran's escalating attacks in the Strait of Hormuz were the week's defining story, sinking two ships and keeping fuel prices high around the world. In Canada, a second straight month of job losses and a trade war with no thaw set the tone, while Alberta heads into Monday's referendum and Ontario cities into their October 26 elections.

top.headline: Iran escalates in the Strait of Hormuz
top.what: About 20 ships have been attacked near the strait since October 1, two sank on October 14, and an Iranian commander now claims the strait is closed. Brent crude spent the week between about $104 and $107 a barrel.
top.why: It is the biggest single driver of fuel and shipping prices this year, including at Ontario gas pumps.

top.headline: Canada lost 68,000 jobs in September
top.what: A second straight monthly drop pushed unemployment to 6.5%. Ontario's rate is 7.0% and youth unemployment is 13%.
top.why: It raises the odds of a Bank of Canada rate cut on October 28.

top.headline: Trade war with the U.S. shows no thaw
top.what: Trump is keeping tariffs even as U.S. polls turn against them. Poilievre toured Michigan to argue for tariff-free trade, and the U.S. ambassador warned Canadian politicians to stay out of the midterms.
top.why: Ontario's auto and steel jobs are the most exposed in the country.

top.headline: Trump's energy truce for Ukraine falls apart
top.what: Russia kept hitting Ukraine's power grid, leaving about 600,000 people without electricity, and Zelenskyy has lifted Ukraine's pause on strikes against Russian refineries. Trump's plan to buy Russian diesel drew criticism from senators of both parties.
top.why: It splits Washington from Kyiv and its allies heading into winter.

top.headline: Houthi strikes shut Riyadh's airport and hit Aramco
top.what: Repeated missile and drone attacks closed King Khalid International Airport and struck Aramco sites. Trump says he would consider joining Saudi strikes after the U.S. midterms.
top.why: A wider war would threaten the Red Sea, the main backup route for oil and container ships.

top.headline: Alberta heads into Monday's referendum
top.what: Albertans answer ten questions, including whether to start a path toward separation. Carney is rallying in Calgary, and Premier Smith says she voted to stay in Canada.
top.why: A strong separatist showing would dominate national politics.

top.headline: Stelco layoffs begin in Hamilton
top.what: Up to 500 jobs are going. Ottawa says owner Cleveland-Cliffs is breaking legally binding job promises, and NDP leaders want the plant nationalized.
top.why: It is the clearest local sign of how the trade war is hitting Ontario industry.
